paper.title: An extended theory of Lucas' functions (the Lucas-Lehmer test for Mersenne numbers)

program.how: written for ounce-core from the Lucas-Lehmer criterion (s_0 = 4, s_(i+1) = s_i^2 - 2 mod 2^p - 1); own multi-word arithmetic on 64-bit limbs, no third-party code copied
program.target: static freestanding aarch64 Linux ELF, run with `ounce-core run-elf`

claims_checked: the Lucas-Lehmer test is applied to all 210 odd primes p <= 1300; exactly the exponents 3, 5, 7, 13, 17, 19, 31, 61, 89, 107, 127, 521, 607, 1279 give a zero residue, which with the base case p = 2 (M_2 = 3) is the published list of 15 Mersenne prime exponents up to 1300; no other exponent in the range passes and none is missed

expected_values_source.what: the list of Mersenne prime exponents (sequence A000043), terms 1 to 15 (2 ... 1279); the data is the published list of exponents, copied as numbers. The 1930 paper itself was not fetched.
expected_values_source.note: the sequence entry lists the exponents found by Lucas, Lehmer, Robinson and later searchers; this check reproduces the list for p <= 1300 only

negative_control: built with -DLL_START=3 (starting value 3 instead of 4), only 9 of the 15 exponents are found (2 3 7 19 31 107 127 607 1279) and the program exits 1
not_checked: Mersenne exponents above 1300 (2203, 2281, ... up to 82589933): too slow for the 2 billion instruction default budget of ounce-core
the proof that the criterion is correct (only its outcome for primes up to 1300)
the p = 2 case is taken as given (M_2 = 3), the Lucas-Lehmer test is stated for odd p
speed figures (emulator run time says nothing about the authors' hardware)
Tier-4 and native ARM64 execution (the native comparison is x86-64)
what_a_pass_means: this program, run on ounce-core, finds exactly the 15 published Mersenne prime exponents up to 1300 by the Lucas-Lehmer test. It does not show that the test works for larger p.
